rationale: `uses` is the class the ontology work shrank from 34,727 edges at 6.0% resolution to 26 at 100%, so the small number is the point: every `uses` edge in this lane has both endpoints resolvable. Three cases are pinned — a forward reference (declared after use), a separate `animation-name` property, and a name this file does NOT declare. The last one is the one that matters: an animation can legitimately come from another stylesheet, and inventing an endpoint for it is the `global` phantom this lane already removed once.

forbidRelationships.comment: a @keyframes name is not an override of itself; the dropped-vendor-discriminator mutant emits this self row

_targetSpelling: CSS-D15: a target that names a declaration THIS file publishes is spelled `<file-scope>::<name>`, where the scope is the file's project-relative path without its extension. The bare spelling stays for a target this file does not declare (a cross-file or external reference) and for `imports`, whose target is another file's module name.
